key_insight: Deep sequence models are more robust than a strong tabular baseline for PV power forecasting when NWP inputs are noisy, because they better filter temporally correlated forecast errors and reweight toward stable historical signals.
engineering_relevance: For PV forecasting systems, robustness should be evaluated alongside nominal accuracy and latency, since model choice under forecast uncertainty can change operational reliability.
method: Physically constrained simulation with virtual PV power to isolate input-error propagation
Dynamic NWP perturbations with clear-sky-dependent heteroscedastic noise and Erbs-consistent radiation reconstruction
Compare six models using accuracy, robustness, and computational latency plus SHAP/IG interpretability
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation of six models, including PatchTST, GRU, N-HITS, and LightGBM, under dynamic NWP perturbations and shows sequence models outperform the tabular baseline under medium to high disturbance.
watch_item: Robustness findings depend on the simulated perturbation design and virtual-response setup, so transfer to real plant deployments should be validated with site-specific error statistics.
paper_title: Robustness of Deep Learning Models for PV Power Forecasting under NWP Forecast Errors: A Spatiotemporal and Physically Interpretable Analysis
